title.narrative: Linking relief, rehabilitation & Dev. through climate sensitive livelihood in Adamawa State

description.narrative: Nigeria is faced with water scarcity and droughts which occur every five years, on average, with the potential to increase in frequency due to climate change. This scenario not only threatens food security, livelihoods, and productivity, but also exacerbates fragility and increases the risk of violence. The drying up of rivers, and particularly the shrinking of Lake Chad is attributable to the effects of climate change and is having a significant impact on conflict-affected population. Climate change poses serious threat to life in rural communities in Northeast Nigeria, particularly in conflict-affected states bordering Cameroun such as Borno and Adamawa. Conflicts over resources and communal violence on limited resources, have killed at least 10,000 Nigerians in less than a decade. A case in point is Nigeria’s frequent farmer-herder conflicts: feed scarcity and water shortages caused partly by desertification and drought have sent nomadic pastoralists, most of them ethnic Fulanis, wandering south, outside their normal grazing routes. For over a decade, the insurgency in Northeast Nigeria has caused severe population movements with large influxes of displaced population seeking safety. As of February 2022, IOM has reported a significant growth of displaced population numbers settling in Adamawa State, particularly in 12 Local Government Areas. With the increase of displaced population, the area has suffered deforestation due to unsustainable charcoal production, and the use of wood for cooking and farming activities. The use of harmful farming practices including an increased use of inorganic fertilizer and chemicals (pesticides and herbicides) on farmlands has contributed to soil erosion and aridity. Rural communities have also resorted to hunting of wild animals for food, also affecting the biodiversity in the area.
